items: Walk through every room in your home with your phone checking WiFi signal strength and document where you get 2 bars or fewer as weak zones
Count every device currently connected to your network including phones, tablets, laptops, smart devices, streaming players, and gaming consoles
Run speed tests in the rooms where your most critical smart devices are located to measure download speed, upload speed, latency, and jitter
Identify which areas of your home have adequate coverage and which areas have dead zones or weak signals that will cause device failures
Create a separate IoT network in your router settings by setting up a second SSID specifically for all your smart home devices
Move all smart devices to the new IoT network while keeping your computers, phones, and work devices on the main network for better security and performance
Upgrade to a mesh router system or add WiFi access points to eliminate dead zones that cause your smart devices to lose connectivity
Upgrade your router if you have more than 30 connected devices or are experiencing persistent congestion and reliability problems on your network
Check the specs and user reviews for any new device you're considering to confirm it supports local control without requiring cloud account registration or internet connectivity
Create a cloud-free device shortlist by researching which products can operate fully offline without requiring account registration or server access
Adjust motion detection sensitivity in your camera app settings to medium or low to reduce false alerts from moving shadows and small animals
Define specific activity zones in your camera app by drawing boundaries around entry points while excluding areas with frequent environmental movement
